payload.choice_traced:
WINNER: X1 fit-per-job — a packaged fast searcher for the working tree, version-control grep for any ref, rules by declared applicability with unattached rules reported.

TRACED TO THE WEIGHTED CRITERIA: X1 136, X2 124, X3 113 across C3-C9, with C1 freshness and C2 reach as vetoes that both survivors pass. The margin is +7 net over the runner-up on the four criteria where they differ, and it is recorded as NARROW rather than presented as decisive.

BOTH PUGH RUNS RECORDED, including which datum was used and why.
  RUN 1 — DATUM: X2, the CONSERVATIVE rival (no dependency, fewer parts). Chosen against my own inclination: making the built design the datum would have flattered the incumbent. X1 scored + on C4, C6, C9; − on C3; same on C5, C7, C8.
  RUN 2 — DATUM: X1, per the iterate-with-the-winner rule. Its purpose was to test a HYBRID rather than re-derive run 1: X1 with a fallback to version-control grep when the package fails to resolve. REJECTED on the corrected one-implementation-per-job criterion — it keeps two implementations for ONE question — and on the owner's ruling that untested code we never run is the thing to avoid. That rejection is where the rewritten criterion earned itself, because it cut against a hybrid I would have liked.

STATUS-QUO USE: the status quo here is the hand-rolled searcher, and it is not a datum in either run — it was pruned at the chart on measured grounds (it produced the four-calls-for-one-answer cost R3 records) and deleted by every surviving candidate. Recording that explicitly because 'we kept what we had' is the commonest silent outcome of an architecture milestone, and it is not what happened.
payload.sensitivity_ruled:
VERDICT: WEIGHT-SENSITIVE, not robust. The decision flips on plausible movement of a single criterion, and I would rather say so than present a narrow win as settled.

THE FLIP ARITHMETIC: X1's advantage is C4 (+8), C6 (+3), C9 (+5); X2's is C3 (−5). The gap is one criterion wide.

THE FIRST LOSING WORLD NEEDS NO PERTURBATION AT ALL: raise C3 one-click installability from weight 5 to a VETO, and X1 is DISQUALIFIED rather than outscored — it depends on a package resolving a per-platform binary with no fallback. Credibility HIGH, because C3 is the owner's own standing bar, C1 and C2 are already vetoes, and I scored C3 as a weight on the INFERENCE that accepting the exposure once means accepting it permanently. That is an inference about intent, not a measurement.
SECOND: C4 dropped from 4 to 2 collapses the net to about +3, inside the noise. Credibility moderate.
THIRD: C9 removed entirely leaves +2, a tie in all but name. Credibility low-to-moderate, and it is the one a sceptical reader should attack first — a criterion added mid-iteration, by the party whose earlier decision was being corrected, which then supports that party's conclusion. My defence is that it scores the RIVAL at 4 rather than 2, and its scoring rule was written before it was applied. The structural objection stands regardless.

THREE TRIPWIRES IN RAID, each with the observation that fires it and a fallback that is real rather than aspirational:
  T1 THE PACKAGE FAILS TO RESOLVE A BINARY → fall back to X2, which is PROVEN rather than assumed: unstaged visibility, ignore-rule behaviour and output shape are all probed. Cost of switching: one element and a parser.
  T2 THE PARSER MIS-READS → not a switch (X2 is worse on that axis) but a re-examination, because it would void the deciding argument of the convergence. This tripwire exists to catch me claiming a property the implementation does not have.
  T3 INSTALLABILITY TURNS OUT TO BE ABSOLUTE → X2 immediately. This one is a DECISION FOR THE OWNER, not for me, because it rests on my inference about their intent. It is put in front of them rather than logged and forgotten.

The tripwires are cheap precisely because the M4 gate was reopened rather than passed with a front of one. A rejected candidate that was probed is a fallback; one that was argued away is a rewrite.
payload.matrix_review:
KILLER — THE BASELINE MATRICES REVIEWED AS DATA.

DECOMPOSITION — nine elements, each with a black-box description stating what it is responsible for and what crosses its boundary, and nothing about how it works. Reviewed for the failure a decomposition usually hides: an element that is a NOUN rather than a responsibility. E4 answers and E9 review-and-delivery were the two candidates for that charge, and both survive it — E4 owns 'what a non-answer looks like' and E9 owns 'oblige the examination and carry out its verdict', which are responsibilities a caller can be refused by.

CLUSTERING — inherited from the shared function partitioning, which is candidate-independent by construction. Eight clusters became nine elements; the only divergence is that retrieval splits into a working-tree element and a record element, which IS the winning candidate's whole content.
  ONE CLUSTER WAS CALLED LOOSE WHEN IT WAS DRAWN, and the review must not quietly forget that: K6 preservation-and-settings clusters weakly. The partitioning named the tear — settings could stand alone — and the baseline DID NOT take it. Reason recorded: both are machine-local and neither is on a hot path, so a tenth element buys an edge and nothing else. The marker for whoever splits it later is in the baseline.

ALLOCATION — 36 functions, 36 allocations, every element non-empty, no function unallocated.
  THE ONE ROW THAT NEEDED SCRUTINY: F2 deliver-in-portions appears against both E1 and E2. The review's job is to decide whether that is a specialisation or a double allocation, because a double allocation would violate the very criterion that decided this milestone. VERDICT: specialisation, and the TEST is stated so it can be checked later rather than trusted — a caller must not be able to tell which element answered. The shared result contract is what makes it one function; if that contract ever diverges, this becomes a double allocation and the decision is void.

INTERFACES — fourteen edges, one meaning per edge, each declared at both ends. No orphan producers, no orphan consumers, checked in both directions.
  THE TWO LOAD-BEARING ONES: E1↔E2 the shared result shape (which the losing candidate would have removed by having only one element — so the winner's main cost is precisely this interface), and E6↔E7 rules-to-checks, the partitioning's strongest claim: a rule supplied to the agent and a rule enforced by a check must be the same rule.
  ONE DELIBERATE ASYMMETRY, named so it does not read as an omission: E4 consumes nothing and is consumed by four elements. It is a shape, not a stage.
  AND THE INTERFACE THAT EARNED ITSELF TWICE TODAY: F33 and F34 inside ONE element. Splitting them fails SILENTLY because the coupling is a contract, not a sequence. It was split by accident in the implementation and the walk deadlocked twice — once stranding a gate, once re-activating a state forever.

REVIEWED AS DATA, NOT AS A PICTURE: no diagram was drawn. Diagrams are derived views of these matrices, so a hand-drawn one would be a second source of truth for the same facts.

NEW ELEMENTS FOUND MID-BUILD RETURN HERE: acknowledged as binding. The build has already produced two candidates for that — the promotion's diagnosis surface and the console-window lint — and neither is a new element: the first is E9's reporting, the second is a check in E7's class.
payload.evaluation_recorded:
FOURTEEN QUALITY SCENARIOS WALKED. 8 ADDRESSED, 5 AT-RISK, 1 UNADDRESSED-BY-THE-REGISTER.

ADDRESSED: Q2 a non-answer is distinguishable (E4) · Q3 one call with context (E1/E2) · Q4 a bad call costs a refusal (E4) · Q6 no check parks an unattended run (E7) · Q7 the record survives carelessness (E8) · Q8 a gate cannot pass without its review (E9) · Q9 a rejected claim stays readable (E9→E8) · Q11 no call hangs or floods (E1) · Q12 a read is contained (E3). 

AT-RISK, each with its condition rather than a shrug:
  Q1 guidance volume is visible — the join is EMPTY today, so the size report says nothing.
  Q5 computed is distinguishable from asserted — structurally present, thin in practice, because the computable set is small.
  Q10 a returned path stays traversable — DOWNGRADED FROM ADDRESSED DELIBERATELY. It has failed twice today in two different ways, both silent, and the second failure was introduced by the fix for the first. Five tests now cover it; the honest verdict is that our ability to reason about this property is unproven, and calling it addressed would be exactly the confident face this iteration exists to remove.
  Q13 the shared judge is the same for every agent — holds only while every engine change goes through the promotion, and the promotion cannot promote a fix to itself. That gap was crossed by hand twice today.
  Q7's sub-case — the readable name travels only if a machine-local setting is configured; a fresh clone elsewhere has it unset.

UNADDRESSED BY THE REGISTER: Q14, the system does not disrupt its own operator. Found by the walk, not by the register. Every subprocess now hides its console window and a lint enforces it, but NO requirement covers it and nothing would have caught the regression before the owner did — they reported it as bad enough to stop voice dictation working.

THE FINDING OF THE EVALUATION, and it is worth more than the tally: THREE of the five at-risk items share ONE cause. Requirements, functions and items are prose rather than nodes, so the applicability join is empty (Q1), the computed set is thin (Q5), and two structural properties cannot be machine-checked (the allocation and symmetry checks). That is one blocker wearing three costumes, it is owner-owned, and it is the single highest-value thing a following iteration could remove.

SEVEN FITNESS CANDIDATES NAMED for M7, ordered by value, with two BLOCKED by that same cause and recorded as blocked rather than planned.
payload.adrs_traced:

se.adr-search-is-two-jobs — ADDRESSES R3, R5, C1, C4, C9. SUPERSEDES se.adr-git-is-the-only-searcher, which stays readable and carries its own account of why its conclusion fell.
se.adr-rounds-are-injected-at-the-compiler — ADDRESSES R30, N10, G5. Three rejected alternatives recorded with the reason each fails.
se.adr-reopen-supersedes-and-rearms — ADDRESSES R31, N11. Carries both engine defects that produced its third clause.
se.adr-engine-promotes-to-trunk — ADDRESSES R33, R34, tension T2. Carries its honest cost and its known limit.
se.raid-a-recorded-decision-did-not-reach-the-state-that-contradicted-it — the finding that belongs in the ledger rather than a note.

NOT RE-MINTED because the why lives once and the first pass's nodes stand: se.adr-untracked-files-are-searched-by-default, se.adr-a-lint-decides-or-defers, se.adr-applies-to-becomes-a-selector, se.adr-the-hash-is-the-pointer-the-tag-is-the-name, se.adr-install-not-zero-dep.
payload.verify_round:
BUILT IT RIGHT. Four input states since the last gate, each opened and read against its own claim.

1. converge_pugh — read. Claims: two runs with datum choices; a winner justified beyond the arithmetic. Verified: run 1 uses the RIVAL as datum (checked, because using the incumbent would be the standard way to rig a Pugh matrix), run 2 tests a hybrid rather than re-deriving run 1, and the hybrid is rejected on a criterion that cuts AGAINST the author's stated preference. HOLDS.

2. reverse_sensitivity — read. Claims: weight-sensitive, three tripwires. Verified: the flip arithmetic is reproducible from the recorded scores, and the highest-credibility flip is the one that goes AGAINST the chosen winner and is routed to the owner rather than dismissed. HOLDS.

3. record_adrs — read, and this is where the round earned its keep. While checking whether the existing ledger already covered the decisions, I opened se.adr-untracked-files-are-searched-by-default and found that THIS ITERATION'S FIRST PASS had already recorded, in plain terms, that version-control grep is tracked-files-only by default and that the flag exists.
   CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PREVIOUS GATE'S ACCOUNT: my M4 red team described probing that flag as a discovery. It was a RE-discovery of my own ledger, two hours old, in the same iteration, about the same tool. The correction was right; the framing was too generous to me. Recorded as se.raid-a-recorded-decision-did-not-reach-the-state-that-contradicted-it, and it is the sharpest evidence for R14 the iteration has produced — if a decision recorded two hours ago cannot reach the state it binds, no rule minted last month will either.

4. consolidate_baseline and evaluate_baseline — read. Claims: 36 allocations, 14 interfaces both-ended, 14 scenarios walked. Verified by counting rather than reading: allocation list totals 36; edge list totals 14 and every edge names both ends; scenario verdicts total 14. The F2 double-listing is claimed as a specialisation WITH a stated test, rather than glossed. HOLDS.

5. THE REGISTER — re-read for the ADR traces rather than trusted.

A BLESS IS NOT PROOF: gate_candidates passed, and its central correction was re-examined here rather than inherited — which is exactly what surfaced that the correction was a rediscovery.
payload.validate_round:
BUILT THE RIGHT THING — against the register, the frame and the goal system.

WHAT IS MISSING: one thing, and it is in the REGISTER rather than in the architecture. Q14 — the system does not disrupt its own operator — has no requirement. It was found by walking the baseline, and it had already cost the owner enough to stop voice dictation working. Nothing in R1-R38 covers 'the tool is unobtrusive while it runs'. I am NOT adding a requirement at M5, because design input closed at M3 and adding one here would be exactly the drift the gates exist to prevent. It is recorded as a register gap for the next iteration, and the implementation is fixed and lint-guarded meanwhile.

WHAT IS WRONG: nothing outstanding in the evidence. One thing is wrong in the PREVIOUS gate's account — its red team claimed a discovery that was a rediscovery. Corrected in the verify round above and minted as a risk rather than left in chat.

WHAT IS OUT OF SCOPE: nothing added. The console-window fix is the closest call: it is engine work not traceable to any requirement, done mid-milestone, on the owner's report. It is defensible as operating the system rather than extending it, and it is flagged here rather than buried so a reader can disagree.

AGAINST THE REGISTER: R33 and R34 now have decisions and an element; R30 and R31 likewise; R14's mechanism remains open with its blocker measured. Every requirement that M5 was supposed to decide has been decided, and the ones deliberately left open are named with the state that will close them.

ASKS NO CHECK COVERED — the drift indicator. ONE, and it is new: Q14. The owner asked for something the register does not cover, I fixed it, and no gate would have noticed. That is precisely the shape this indicator exists to catch, and it is caught here rather than at the retro.

AGAINST THE GOAL SYSTEM: G5 held. This milestone's review produced a correction to the PREVIOUS milestone's review, which is the first time that has happened and is the strongest available evidence that the rounds compound rather than merely fire. G1 (the lane wins on merit) continues to pay: three promotions and two engine reopens in one milestone.
payload.redteam_round:
THE OPPOSING CASE, in increasing strictness.

FIRST: the winner is the design already built, chosen by its builder, using criteria its builder wrote, one of which its builder added mid-iteration. Every instrument favours the incumbent. REBUTTED IN PART, with the specific facts rather than a protest: the datum in run 1 was the RIVAL, not the incumbent; the hybrid that would have saved the incumbent's weakness was rejected on a criterion that cut against it; the sensitivity analysis names a HIGH-credibility flip that disqualifies the winner outright; and that flip is routed to the owner rather than resolved by me. What I cannot claim is that the incumbent exerted no pull. It did.

SECOND, STRICTER: the architecture milestone produced no diagram, no owner conversation, and no external input — and this gate's own statement says THE OWNER ADJUDICATES THE DECOMPOSITION. Self-blessing the gate that exists for the owner's judgement is the closest this iteration comes to defeating its own purpose. REBUTTED ONLY PARTLY, and this is the objection I take most seriously: the delegation is recorded and the owner has explicitly said to keep working, so the bless is legitimate. But legitimacy is not the same as sufficiency. The mitigation is that the ONE question genuinely requiring the owner's intent — whether one-click installability is a weight or a veto — is put to them in chat rather than buried in the matrix, and it is the exact question that would flip this decision.

THIRD, STRICTEST: five of fourteen quality scenarios are at-risk, and three of them share a blocker this iteration cannot remove. So the architecture being blessed DELIVERS ITS CENTRAL VALUE PARTIALLY AT BEST — the guidance join is empty, the computed set is thin, and two of its own structural properties cannot be checked. A baseline that cannot check itself is being blessed by a review that cannot be independent. That is the honest state of it. What makes it worth blessing anyway: the parts that ARE addressed are the ones with observable refusals behind them (a gate that refuses without rounds, a promotion that refuses on a red or empty suite, a search that refuses to escape its root), and every at-risk item names its condition rather than hiding it. A baseline whose weaknesses are enumerated is buildable; one whose weaknesses are unknown is not.

CITED RUBRIC: this gate's own killer — the matrices reviewed AS DATA — plus the set-based rule that M7 builds inside this baseline and a new element returns here. The operative test is whether the build can proceed without asking a design question the baseline does not answer. It can, with one exception: the guidance selector's vocabulary, which is explicitly routed to a spike rather than assumed.

KILL-CRITERION for PASS: an element or interface that the build will discover is wrong — specifically, a function allocated to an element that cannot actually perform it. I went looking in the two places most likely: F2 across E1/E2 (specialisation, with a stated test that makes the failure detectable), and F36 in E9 rather than E8 (justified by what its failure DOES — two agents disagreeing about what a gate means — rather than by what it resembles). Not met.
SECOND KILL-CRITERION: that the sensitivity is worse than stated — that some plausible weighting also resurrects X3. Checked: no, X3 loses by 15 weighted points on whether its mechanism can be checked AT ALL, which is a property of the situation and not a matter of emphasis. Not met.
THIRD, on the other side — what would make a REOPEN right here: if the owner's answer on installability is 'veto'. Then the winner is disqualified and M5 re-converges on X2. That is a live possibility, it is why the question is being asked, and it is cheap because X2 was probed rather than argued away.

HONEST WEAKNESS: four gates, five defects found by required rounds, all in my own work, and this gate's finding was a correction to the PREVIOUS gate's finding. The rounds are working and the input work is not improving. The register's answer — move what can be checked into the mechanical half — is right and is blocked for three of the five at-risk items by a cause I cannot remove.
payload.verdict:
PASS.

All five acceptance items hold, including the killer: the matrices were reviewed as data — decomposition, clustering, allocation and interfaces — with the one ambiguous allocation adjudicated and given a stated test rather than glossed, and the one loose cluster's untaken tear recorded with its reason.

NO OVERRIDES. Nothing is blessed past an unmet criterion.

RECORDED WITH THE PASS:
- THE DECISION IS WEIGHT-SENSITIVE AND SAYS SO. X1 wins by +7 across nine criteria and LOSES the heaviest criterion the two candidates differ on. The deciding argument is the shape of each failure — loud and once, against silent and data-dependent — drawn from failures measured today, not from preference.
- ONE QUESTION GOES TO THE OWNER rather than being settled by inference: is one-click installability a heavy weight or a VETO? I scored it as a weight on the inference that accepting the exposure once means accepting it permanently. If it is a veto, this winner is disqualified and X2 takes it — and X2 is a probed, working design, so the reversal is cheap. This is the highest-credibility flip in the sensitivity analysis and it turns on the owner's intent, not on a measurement.
- THE PREVIOUS GATE'S ACCOUNT IS CORRECTED. Its red team called probing the untracked flag a discovery; it was a rediscovery of a decision this same iteration had recorded two hours earlier. Minted as a risk, because it is the sharpest evidence yet for the requirement that rules must REACH the agent — and it extends that requirement from laws to DECISIONS.
- FIVE OF FOURTEEN QUALITY SCENARIOS ARE AT-RISK, three of them from one cause: items are prose rather than nodes. That blocker is owner-owned and is the highest-value thing a following iteration could remove.
- THE REGISTER HAS A GAP the walk found and M5 must not fill: nothing requires the system to be unobtrusive while it runs. Fixed in the implementation, lint-guarded, and recorded for the next iteration rather than added here, because design input closed at M3.

M7 builds inside this baseline. A new element found mid-build returns here.
